waves.name: Utility and admin jobs
waves.rationale: Jobs that run no application program and touch no shared data. Proves the pipeline and the job-runner replacement at no business risk. FTPJCL holds a clear-text credential, so this wave also removes it.
waves.unblocks: The job runner and deployment path that every later wave uses.

waves.name: Read-only extract batch
waves.rationale: Programs that read the master files and write nothing another entry point uses. They are the first place the new platform must read the VSAM record layouts byte for byte.
waves.unblocks: Verified readers for the account, card, customer and cross-reference layouts that waves 5 and 6 depend on.

waves.name: Online inquiry screens
waves.rationale: Read-only screens. The sign-on, menu and admin menu are one strongly connected component and COTRN00C and COTRN01C are another, so they move whole. COTRN00C and COTRN01C are god modules and go behind a facade.
waves.unblocks: The screen navigation layer that wave 7 reuses.

waves.name: Build and data-definition jobs
waves.rationale: Compile procs and generation-data-group definitions. They stop mattering once the build is replaced. The INTRDRJ jobs are retirement candidates.
waves.unblocks: The new build toolchain. It is a chore for the business and unblocks no named business capability.

waves.name: Reference-data loads and the CICS file handshake
waves.rationale: Batch writers whose datasets no other batch entry point writes. Holds the CLOSEFIL and OPENFIL jobs that wave 6 depends on, so the handshake must be replaced here. CARDFILE leaves this wave for wave 6, see deviations. CBSTM03A is the hardest program in the tree and its output is regenerable, so it is rewritten last in the wave.
waves.unblocks: The CICS close and open handshake and the reference-data loaders used by wave 6.

waves.name: Posting, master refresh and transaction report
waves.rationale: All three must-not-break items live here. It has 30 units but one sentence describes it: the batch ledger cycle. I did not cut it. CBTRN02C and CBACT04C both update the account and category-balance files, so a cut would leave two writers of one file split across waves. It is sequenced inside the wave in the wave plan instead. Confidence cannot be high: CORPT00C makes a computed call, the CA-7 listing that triggers POSTTRAN was not parsed, and nothing in the tree produces the daily transaction input.
waves.unblocks: Daily posting, the master refresh and the transaction report on the new platform. The online writers in wave 7 then become the only second writer of the account and transaction files.

waves.name: Online maintenance and payment screens
waves.rationale: Online programs that write the account, card, transaction and user-security files. Last of the VSAM waves because every one shares a file with wave 6 batch. COBIL00C and COTRN02C each assign the next transaction id as last key plus one, which collides with batch posting if both run.
waves.unblocks: Retires the second writer of the account and transaction files, so the legacy VSAM and the CICS handshake can go.

waves.name: Authorization and unload subsystem
waves.rationale: Touches IMS, DB2 and MQ. The extractor reads none of the IMS DBD or PSB files or the DB2 DDL, so the data model of this wave is unread. CBPAUP0J triggers POSTTRAN in the CA-7 listing, so the scheduler link to wave 6 must be kept.

waves.name: Authorization screens and transaction-type DB2
waves.rationale: DB2 and IMS screens. COPAUS0C and COPAUS1C are one strongly connected component and COPAUS0C is a god module, so it goes behind a facade.
waves.unblocks: Retires the last DB2 and IMS dependencies.

unassigned.reason: No static edge reaches it and 28 computed calls could. It stays unplaced and in the unknown dead-code bucket.

deviations.reason: Must-not-break item: the account and card master refresh. ACCTFILE (wave 6) and CARDFILE run back to back in one wrapper, so the refresh would otherwise straddle two waves and have no single testable boundary.
